items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: I liked classical music. I loved Claudio Monteverdi’s operas and masses

ctx.x: I’m letting that sink in for a moment. Because I’m somewhat familiar with those two gentlemen.

Well I was hoping to use names that would mean something to you. I wasn’t going to resort to my hillbilly music universe because I don’t know how far you go in that direction. But the same thing holds true there. I grew up in Washington which was a — it wasn’t in the north, it wasn’t in the south, but it was where those two influences tended to evolve and so you could hear everything from — the richest on the radio from a cappella black Gospel to rhythm & blues to honky tonk country to early bluegrass. And you’d…

I’m picturing you in your physical moves over the years. I remember in college we would have our boxes of LPs and then I have accepted a few collections of 78s here. And when I went to move them I was reminded of how fast technology moves with recording mediums.
